Hi Jarrett,

Sure, I think you just want to change the width options of tidy.
add the command:

   options(width = 75)

into your first chunk and that should do it.

(the option tidy=true is set on chunks be default, and linewraps at 72
characters, which is often too wide for slides).

-Carl

messages.subject: Using knitr with \tikzexternalize?
messages.body_plain:
I've been using knitr to output my diagrams to dev='tikz' for a few months now. This all works fine. However, some of my plots are quite large and the resulting pdf becomes pretty big (and refuses to print on some printers). What I'd really like to do is to convert the pdf images rendered by tikzDevice into some other format such as png. The pgf/tikz library already supports this sort of behaviour with its external library (see the pgf manual (pdf) page 354). <http://texdoc.net/texmf-dist/doc/generic/pgf/pgfmanual.pdf> Whenever I use the \tikzexternalize command in the .Rnw file that I'm knitting I run into errors. The problem seems to be when calculating string widths the tikz generated is invalid.

Before I try to pair my thesis down into a minimum working example recreating this problem I'd like to know if anyone has successfully used the tikz external library with knitr. Or alternatively if there is a simpler way of retaining nicely formatted tikzDevice plots but incorporating them as rasterised images?

messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Using knitr with \tikzexternalize?
messages.body_plain:
That is basically a call to ImageMagick (convert), and you can do the
same thing in R by calling system('convert foo.pdf foo.png').

It has been asked once in this mailing list, and here is an example of
PNG produced from tikz/PDF:
http://theanalysisofdata.com/probability/3_1.html

But for LaTeX, it is a little bit different. I have been thinking for
a long time about a post-processing hook function for plot files, so
that you can do anything to your plots. I'll probably add it soon.
Before that, you can manually call ImageMagick to convert PDF to PNG,
and give higher priority to PNG, e.g.

\DeclareGraphicsExtensions{.png,.pdf,.jpg}

Regards,
